row.raw_extracted_text: Trends and Demographics Household Tax Analyses Household Taxation Trends The following analyses illustrate the impact of selected County taxes on the typical household from FY 2021 to FY 2027. The Real Estate Tax analysis includes the adopted FY 2027 Real Estate tax rate of $1.12 per $100 of assessed value, which is a 0.25-cent reduction from the FY 2026 rate of $1.1225.

FY 2027 Adopted Budget Facts. On average, residential annual Real Estate tax bills will increase $336.68 in FY 2027 based on the adopted Real Estate Tax rate of $1.12 per $100 of assessed value. The Commercial/Industrial percentage of the County's Real Estate Tax base is 14.42 percent.

Specifically, the FY 2027 budget decreases the Real Estate Tax Rate from $1.1225 to $1.12 per $100, a quarter cent decrease from FY 2026. This rate allows us to provide an additional $117.7 million to FCPS over the FY 2026 Adopted Budget.

The Real Estate Tax rate to be approved by the Board will decrease from $1.1225 per $100 of assessed value to $1.12 per $100 of assessed value. The Personal Property Tax rate will remain at $4.57 per $100 of assessed value for most classes of personal property. In addition, the Stormwater fee will remain at $0.0325 per $100 of assessed value.

DATE: May 4, 2026 TO: Board of Supervisors FROM: Bryan J. Hill County Executive SUBJECT: Adoption of the FY 2027 Budget Plan Attached for your review are the following documents: Board revenue and expenditure adjustments approved at the Budget Mark-up on April 28, 2026 (Attachment I); Resolution Adopting Tax Rates for FY 2027 (Attachment II); FY 2027 Appropriation Resolution for County Agencies/Funds (Attachment III); FY 2027 Appropriation Resolution for School Board Funds (Attachment IV); FY 2027 Fiscal Planning Resolution (Attachment V); and FY 2027 General Fund Statement; FY 2027 General Fund Expenditures by Agency; FY 2027 Expenditures by Fund, Appropriated; and FY 2027 Expenditures by Fund, NonAppropriated (Attachment VI). The attachments noted above provide the official documentation of the adjustments made by the Board of Supervisors on April 28, 2026, associated with the markup of the FY 2027 budget. It should  be  noted  that  the  Board  took  final  action  on  the  FY  2027-2031  Capital  Improvement Program during budget mark-up on April 28. The Real Estate Tax rate to be approved by the Board will decrease from $1.1225 per $100 of assessed value to $1.12 per $100 of assessed value. The Personal Property Tax rate will remain at $4.57 per $100 of assessed value for most classes of personal property. In addition, the Stormwater fee will remain at $0.0325 per $100 of assessed value. Approval of the FY 2027 Appropriation Resolutions, the FY 2027 Fiscal Planning Resolution, and the FY 2027 Resolution Adopting Tax Rates will result in a FY 2027 General Fund Disbursement level of $5.97 billion, which is an increase of $79.39 million, or 1.4 percent, from the FY 2026 Revised Budget Plan and an increase of $259.77 million, or 4.5 percent, over the FY 2026 Adopted Budget Plan.

In FY 2027, General Fund revenue is expected to increase 3.61 percent compared to the FY 2026 Revised Budget Plan . The revenue increase is primarily due to a 3.77 percent increase in the Real Estate assessment base, partially offset by a 0.25-cent decrease in the adopted Real Estate tax rate from  $1.1225  per  $100  of  assessed  value  in  FY  2026  to  $1.12  per  $100  of  assessed  value  in FY 2027. In addition, Personal Property Taxes are projected to increase 3.1 percent due to expected growth in vehicle volume and levy.

As  reflected  in  the  preceding  table,  FY 2027  General  Fund  revenues  are  projected  to  be $5,963,108,250, a decrease of $15,459,065 or 0.3 percent from the FY 2027 Advertised Budget Plan. The decrease is primarily the result of the adoption of a Real Estate tax rate of $1.12 per $100 of assessed value, a 0.25-cent reduction from the advertised rate of $1.1225 per $100 of assessed value, and the allocation of the equivalent of an additional quarter penny on the Real Estate Tax rate, or $8,788,269, to Fund 30300, Affordable Housing Development and Investment. These adjustments are fully described in the following pages.

February 17, 2026 Honorable Board of Supervisors County of Fairfax Chairman and Board Members: I  present the FY 2027 Advertised Budget Plan with a sense of pride, a renewed optimism, and a clear  recognition  that  significant  fiscal  challenges  remain. Two months ago, we presented a joint fiscal forecast to the Board of Supervisors and the School Board. At  that  time,  preliminary  real  estate  projections  indicated  overall  revenue  growth  of  3.0 percent,  driven  by  appreciation  in  residential  property  values  and  partially  offset  by  anticipated declines in commercial values. The FY 2027 Advertised Budget Plan is balanced at the current Real Estate Tax rate of $1.1225 per $100 of assessed value and includes increased support for Fairfax County Public Schools, funding of the County's collective bargaining agreements, and targeted  County  reductions  of  $32.9  million.

February 17, 2026 Honorable Board of Supervisors County of Fairfax Chairman and Board Members: I  present the FY 2027 Advertised Budget Plan with a sense of pride. The FY 2027 Advertised Budget Plan is balanced at the current Real Estate Tax rate of $1.1225 per $100 of assessed value and includes increased support for Fairfax County Public Schools.

The billing rates for both Sewer Service Charges and Base Charges will increase in FY 2027. The Base Charge will increase from $52.62 per quarter to $55.78 per quarter. The Sewer Service Charge will increase from $9.33 to $9.88 per 1,000 gallons of water consumed based on Fairfax County's winter quarter average consumption of 16,000 gallons. In addition, as part of the FY 2020 Adopted Budget Plan, the Board of Supervisors approved the establishment of charges to recover a portion of the cost of disposal and treatment of hauled wastewater at the County's septage receiving facility (SRF).

The five-year sewer rate plan, approved by the Board of Supervisors as part of the FY 2026 Adopted Budget Plan, proposed to increase the sewer charges by 5.9 percent in FY 2027. After careful review, the Wastewater Management staff recommended increasing the sewer charges by 5.9 percent in FY 2027 as previously planned. The Sewer Service Charge  increased  from  $9.33  to  $9.88  per  1,000  gallons  of  water  consumed. The industry practice for a fixed charge revenue rate is 25 percent to 30 percent of operating revenues. The fixed charge revenue percentage in FY 2027 is equal to 25.5  percent.
